high.title: [Hon Hai (Foxconn) June Revenue Hits Record High for the Month, AI Server Cabinet Shipments Drive Growth; Q3 Outlook Remains Strong]
high.summary:
Hon Hai (2317) reported June consolidated revenue of NT$821.76 billion, the strongest June on record, driving both Q2 and H1 2026 revenues to all-time highs for their respective periods. On a year-over-year basis, June revenue surged 52.1%, although it declined 4.3% month-on-month. Q2 consolidated revenue reached NT$2.51 trillion, up 182% quarter-on-quarter and 39.8% year-on-year. H1 2026 consolidated revenue totaled NT$4.64 trillion, up 34.9% year-on-year.

The primary growth driver remains AI server cabinet shipments, where demand continues to expand, though raw material supply tightness is a noted constraint. ICT products are entering the seasonally strong H2 period. Management guided for Q3 to deliver both sequential and year-on-year growth.

high.title: Hon Hai (Foxconn) Revenue: June Revenue NT$821.8B — Monthly, Q2, and H1 All Hit New Historical Highs
high.summary:
Hon Hai (2317) reported June 2026 revenue of NT$821.8 billion, down 4.38% month-on-month but up 52.11% year-on-year, marking the highest June revenue on record. Q2 2026 revenue reached NT$2.51 trillion, up 18.02% QoQ and 39.83% YoY — again a record for any second quarter. Cumulative H1 2026 revenue stood at NT$4.64 trillion, up 34.99% YoY, also a record.

The primary growth driver is robust AI server rack demand, with cloud/network product and component categories showing strong YoY momentum. Management guided Q3 to deliver both QoQ and YoY growth, citing continued AI cabinet demand and seasonal strength in ICT products, though flagged ongoing global geopolitical uncertainty as a risk factor.

medium.title: [Largan Precision June Revenue Falls 19% MoM; Smartphone Peak Season Approaching with iPhone 18 Expected in September — H2 Outlook Cautiously Positive]
medium.summary:
Largan Precision (3008) reported June consolidated revenue of NT$3.712 billion, down 19% month-on-month and 10% year-on-year, reflecting a sequential pullback after stronger earlier months. Q2 consolidated revenue declined 12% quarter-on-quarter but rose 17% year-on-year; H1 2026 revenue reached NT$29.209 billion, up 11% versus the prior year period. Management noted that July order momentum is expected to improve modestly over June, as the smartphone industry enters its traditional peak season ahead of the iPhone 18 launch anticipated in September. Chairman Lin En-ping previously indicated Q4 will be the busiest quarter of the year. An online investor conference is scheduled for July 9th, where attention will focus on Largan's Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) roadmap, including competitive dynamics with Corning's newly unveiled GlassBridge glass optical interconnect technology targeting CPO and glass-core semiconductor packaging architectures. **Market Implications:** Near-term revenue softness is seasonal and largely anticipated; the H2 recovery thesis hinges on iPhone 18 ramp. CPO positioning is a key longer-term watch item for investors.

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Market Super Earnings Season Kicks Off — Bullish Sentiment Targets 50,000-Point Breakthrough
medium.summary: Major institutional brokers including Fubon, Yuanta, Taishin, and Uni-President are cautiously optimistic on Taiwan equities for July, despite recent volatility driven by AI computing capacity concerns. The consensus view is that the index will challenge the 50,000-point level, supported by a packed earnings season. TSMC's June revenue (due July 10) is the key near-term catalyst — analysts estimate if TSMC exceeds NT$440 billion in monthly revenue, Q2 EPS could hit a new record, with H1 EPS projected at NT$48–49. TSMC's investor conference is scheduled for July 16, followed by Tesla, Google, and Intel. Rotation between AI and non-tech sectors is expected to accelerate.

medium.title: New Quarterly Earnings Conference Season Begins This Week — AI Bellwether Stocks to Lead
medium.summary: Taiwan's Q2 2026 earnings conference season begins this week, led by AI-related names. Key dates include Delta Electronics (2308) on July 8, Largan Precision (3008) on July 9, Nanya Technology (2408) on July 10, and TSMC (2330) on July 16. Taiwan Futures Index night session closed at 47,116, suggesting a potential reclaim of the 47K level. Notable: Samsung is reportedly pushing for a 20%+ DRAM price hike in Q3 following prior-quarter increases of 90% and 50%, making Nanya Technology a focus for memory sector bulls. TSMC remains the dominant weight at NT$63.4 trillion market cap.

medium.title: Winbond Electronics & Phison Electronics: Focus on Long-Duration Warrants Amid Memory Sector Rally
medium.summary:
Taiwan's equity market has continued its strong upward momentum, surging 2,208 points last week. Warrant issuers are highlighting Winbond Electronics (2344) and Phison Electronics (8299) as key plays on the memory sector. According to TrendForce estimates, DDR2 contract prices are expected to rise 55–60% in Q2 and a further 35–40% in Q3, extending Q1's strong gains. The supply-demand imbalance is being driven by major DRAM manufacturers reallocating capacity toward HBM and server applications, constraining supply of legacy nodes (DDR4/DDR3/DDR2). Traditional DRAM contract price growth for Q3 is now projected at 20–30% quarter-on-quarter, above prior forecasts of 10–20%. For the second half of 2026, the AI-driven long-cycle seller's market is expected to persist, with demand expanding across AI servers, inference computing, eSSD, high-capacity server DRAM, and LPDDR. Phison is seen as a key beneficiary of AI storage infrastructure and enterprise SSD trends.
